topics.title: Trigonometry I
topics.subject: mathematics
outcomes: Derive sine, cosine and tangent functions from the unit circle. (k, u, s)
Read and use calculators to find values of trigonometric functions. (u, s)
Use sine, cosine and tangent in calculating lengths of sides and angles of right-angled triangles. (u)
Find angles of elevation and depression. (k, s)

body.text: In a right-angled triangle, for a chosen angle θ (not the right angle), the side opposite θ, the side adjacent to θ, and the hypotenuse (the longest side) define three ratios: sine, cosine and tangent.

A ladder leans against a wall, making a 40° angle with the ground, and reaches 3 m up the wall. To find the ladder's length (the hypotenuse), use sine, since the wall height is opposite the 40° angle: sin(40°) = 3 ÷ length, so length = 3 ÷ sin(40°) ≈ 3 ÷ 0.643 ≈ 4.67 m.

An angle of elevation is measured upward from the horizontal (e.g. looking up at the top of a building); an angle of depression is measured downward from the horizontal (e.g. looking down at a boat from a cliff). From a lighthouse 50 m tall, the angle of depression to a boat 600 m away (measured horizontally) satisfies tan(θ) = 50 ÷ 600, so θ = tan⁻¹(50/600) ≈ 4.76°.
